mission_02: Prototypical Networks, introduced by Snell et al. (2017), are a metric-based meta-learning approach for few-shot classification. The core idea is simple yet powerful: for each class in the support set, compute a prototype (mean embedding) in a learned metric space. Classification of query points is done by computing distances to each prototype and applying softmax over negative distances. The embedding function f_θ is trained end-to-end to produce representations where examples of the same class cluster tightly around their prototype. Training uses episodic sampling: each episode samples N classes with K support examples and Q query examples per class (N-way K-shot). The loss is cross-entropy over the prototype-based classification probabilities. Prototypical networks are computationally efficient, require no inner loop optimization at test time, and have become a standard baseline for few-shot learning.
